notes.text: Yet — Although he miscarried in the matter of high places, yet in the general, his heart was right with God. Statutes - According to the statutes or commands of God, which are here called the statutes of David; not only because they were diligently practiced by David, but also because the observation of them was so earnestly pressed upon Solomon, and fortified with David's authority and command.

Truth — In the true worship of God, in the profession, belief, practice and defense of the true religion. So truth here contains all duties to God, as righteousness doth his duties to men, and uprightness the right manner of performing both sorts of duties. With thee - That is, in thy judgment, to whom he often appealed as the witness of his integrity.

Child — So he was in years: not above twenty years old; and withal (which he principally intends) he was raw and unexperienced, as a child, in state affairs. Go out, &c. - To govern my people, and manage affairs.

In the midst — Is set over them to rule and guide them. A metaphor from the overseer of divers workmen, who usually is in the midst of them, that he may the better observe how each of them discharges his office. Chosen - Thy peculiar people, whom thou takest special care of, and therefore wilt expect a more punctual account of my government of them.

An understanding heart — Whereby I may both clearly discern, and faithfully perform all the parts of my duty: for both these are spoken of in scripture, as the effects of a good understanding; and he that lives in the neglect of his duties, or the practice of wickedness, is called a fool, and one void of understanding. Discern - Namely in causes and controversies among my people; that I may not through mistake, or prejudice, or passion, give wrong sentences, and call evil good, or good evil. Absalom, that was a fool, wished himself a judge: Solomon, that was a wise man, trembles at the undertaking. The more knowing and considerate men are, the more jealous they are of themselves.
All thy days — Whereby he signifies that these gifts of God were not transient, as they were in Saul, but such as should abide with him whilst he lived.
And if — This caution God gives him, lest his wisdom should make him proud, careless, or presumptuous.

glossa.text: *Solomon therefore went.* In Gabaon was the greatest high place, where was the tabernacle which Moses made, and the brazen altar, upon which Solomon, offering a thousand victims, deserved a divine oracle.

*But if thou wilt walk in my ways,* etc. Without the keeping of God's commandments no man can attain long days, that is, blessedness.

((GREG., lib. VIII Moral., cap. 17.)) After the Lord lights up the darkness of our error with the light of his own knowledge, etc., *as far as* that we may be reformed unto the substance of the incorruption that is promised.

((HIER., epist. 131, tom. I.)) Some think that this is to be understood of the Synagogue and the Church, etc., *as far as* it is also to be noted what the Church saith against the Synagogue.

notes.text: Sought — Diligently meditated upon.
Work — Either all his works, or that eminent branch of those works, his providence towards his people. Righteousness - His justice or faithfulness in performing his word.
Remembered — By their own nature, and the lasting benefits flowing from them, which are such as cannot easily be forgotten.
Meat — All necessary provisions for their being and well-being.

The works — All that he doth on the behalf of his people, or against their enemies. Truth - Are exactly agreeable to his promises, and to justice. Commandments - His laws given to the Israelites, especially the moral law. Sure - Constant and unchangeable.
Done — Constituted or ordered.

Redemption — The deliverance out of Egypt, which was a type of that higher redemption by Christ. Commanded - Appointed, or established firmly by his power and authority. For ever - Through all successive generations of his people to the end of the world. Reverend - Terrible to his enemies, venerable in his peoples eyes, and holy in all his dealings with all men.

The fear — True religion. Beginning - Is the only foundation of, and introduction to, true wisdom. This also is an alphabetical psalm. We have here the character and blessedness of the righteous, ver. 1-9. The iniquity of the wicked, ver. 10.

glossa.text: *I will give praise.* ((AUG.)) Here there is no confession of sins, but of praise: the one mourns, this rejoices: the one shows the wound to the physician, this gives thanks for health. *In the council.* Not rashly, but out of reason, namely for things eternal, as all the just do. ((CASS.)) *In the council of the just.* Here never among all the just, where the wicked are mingled with them, but they are seen already to sing in the fellowship to come, caught up by hope to the things above. *In the council,* which is, when they judge with the Lord. *In the congregation,* when they are gathered together out of the whole.

*Great works.* This is the matter and the cause of the confession. Great are the works of the Lord, in that he makes a godly man out of an ungodly. *Sought out.* ((AUG., CASS.)) To which nothing is like, while he suffers the devil to rage, etc., *as far as* not: *for his justice remaineth for ever and ever. Unto all the wills.* ((AUG.)) Nothing surpasses the will of God, who, even if he wills that thou sin not, yet does not prevent it. If he wills to spare the penitent, he wills also to punish the impenitent; so concerning man God always fulfils his own will, because man does nothing out of which God does not work what he wills.

*Confession and magnificence is his work.* ((CASS.)) As it were: I will give praise, because great are the works of the Lord. Any works soever are also great, if in them there be seen the intention and the will, which is the *confession* of sins, and the *magnificence* of good works: and *justice,* that is, the reward which is justly given.

*He hath made a remembrance.* ((ID.)) Secondly he says that the faithful are filled with a plentiful gift, promising the coming of the Lord, that the inheritance may be eagerly sought. ((AUG.)) *He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works.* Humbling this man and exalting that, etc., *as far as* what shall he receive, he is glorified *glorificatur*; read *glorificatus*, "glorified", in the things to come?

*He hath given food.* ((CASS.)) He makes confession and magnificence, etc., *as far as* that all things may be fulfilled. *He will be mindful,* etc. ((AUG.)) Nor did he give the whole who gave a pledge, etc., *as far as* they enter through the piercing straits of the passion.

*The power of the works.* ((CASS.)) The power of the works is that the blind see, etc. Which things he made known to the Christian people. *That he may give them the inheritance,* this was the intent of the miracles, that they might believe.

*That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles.* ((ID.)) As it were: although he gives them the inheritance, yet they shall suffer many things. *The works of his hands.* ((ID.)) That is, of his power. *Truth,* while he restores to the converted what was promised: *Judgment,* which he threatens to the ungodly. ((AUG.)) *Truth,* which the holy martyrs hold, and for which they are also judged here; *and judgment,* whereby in time to come they shall judge those by whom they are here judged. ((ID.)) *The works of his hands are truth and judgment.* Let *truth* be held by those who are judged, etc., *as far as* this is the inheritance of the New Testament.

*All the commandments are faithful.* ((CASS.)) Because they keep those who keep them, they are not lies. *Confirmed.* Not sent forth in vain, as human words are: *Made,* not only spoken, *in truth,* because all are fulfilled.

*In equity.* ((AUG.)) Because all things are done with the balance of justice.

*He hath sent redemption.* ((CASS.)) Thirdly he affirms the redeemed, and the New Testament consecrated by eternal grace; or. *His name: the beginning of wisdom.* ((ID.)) That is, the Son, who in his humanity is *holy,* in the power of the Godhead *terrible.* Let the advocate therefore be loved, let the judge be feared, lest thou be negligent, lest thou despair.

The fear of the Lord. ((ID.)) The dread of judgment is the gate of conversion, if the discernment of love be added to it. *His praise continueth.* The intent of the psalm, whence Alleluia is prefixed, began with praise and ends in praise: the faithful people, delivered from the devil and giving thanks, has expressed what is to be done here also by the devout, and to be accomplished in heaven: here because he delivers, there because he crowns.

notes.text: Circumspectly — Exactly, with the utmost accuracy, getting to the highest pitch of every point of holiness. Not as fools - Who think not where they are going, or do not make the best of their way.

With all possible care redeeming the time — Saving all you can for the best purposes; buying every possible moment out of the hands of sin and Satan; out of the hands of sloth, ease, pleasure, worldly business; the more diligently, because the present are evil days, days of the grossest ignorance, immorality, and profaneness.
What the will of the Lord is — In every time, place, and circumstance.
Wherein is excess — That is, which leads to debauchery of every kind. But be ye filled with the Spirit - In all his graces, who gives a more noble pleasure than wine can do.

Speaking to each other — By the Spirit. In the Psalms - Of David. And hymns - Of praise. And spiritual songs - On any divine subject. By there being no inspired songs, peculiarly adapted to the Christian dispensation, as there were to the Jewish, it is evident that the promise of the Holy Ghost to believers, in the last days, was by his larger effusion to supply the lack of it. Singing with your hearts - As well as your voice. To the Lord - Jesus, who searcheth the heart.

Giving thanks — At all times and places. And for all things - Prosperous or adverse, since all work together for good. In the name of, or through, our Lord Jesus Christ - By whom we receive all good things.

glossa.text: *Redeeming the time.* That is, what you have done less in one time, restore in another, halving the days which the wicked do not halve. For some halve, others fill up the days, others do not even begin; that is, some die in Egypt, some in the desert, some in the holy land. Nor is it a wonder if you have done less, since the days are evil, nor can all things be done at pleasure.

notes.text: If any eat of this bread — That is, believe in me: he shall live forever - In other words, he that believeth to the end shall be saved. My flesh which I will give you - This whole discourse concerning his flesh and blood refers directly to his passion, and but remotely, if at all, to the Lord's Supper.
Observe the degrees: the Jews are tried here; the disciples, ver. 60-66, the apostles, ver. 67.
Unless ye eat the flesh of the Son of man — Spiritually: unless ye draw continual virtue from him by faith. Eating his flesh is only another expression for believing.
Meat — drink indeed - With which the soul of a believer is as truly fed, as his body with meat and drink.
I live by the Father — Being one with him. He shall live by me -Being one with me. Amazing union!
This is — That is, I am the bread - Which is not like the manna your fathers ate, who died notwithstanding.

glossa.text: *And the bread,* etc. He determines how he is bread, not only according to the Word by which all things live, but also according to the flesh taken up for the life of the world. For human flesh, which was liable to sin and therefore dead, being united to his clean flesh, incorporated, made one with him, lives by his spirit, as the body lives by its own spirit: but he who is not of the body of Christ does not live by the spirit of Christ. But because the Jews were not of this unity, they strove; nor is it expounded to such men how the Lord gives his flesh to be eaten, but he heard, whence they are the more moved.

*Unless you eat the flesh,* etc. ((AUG.)) He wishes this food and drink to be understood as fellowship, etc., *as far as* that from many grains there may be one bread, and from many berries the wine flows together.

*He that eateth.* Certain holy men expound this of the eating of the altar, and they say well; but they ask how it may be unto life everlasting, since for some it is unto death, as the Apostle says. If any man eats at the altar with this eating of which he here treats, namely with faith working and with love, he eats unto life everlasting. But if any man eats otherwise, unto death.

*For the flesh.* Truly the soul and the body shall live from this food, because *my flesh is meat indeed.* Which alone makes men immortal, so that they shall neither hunger nor thirst; another food does not afford this, even if this be sought in it.

*He that eateth.* Now he expounds how that comes to pass which he said, and what it is to eat the flesh and to drink the blood: that is, to abide in Christ and to have Christ abiding in oneself. But he who does not abide in Christ, and in whom Christ does not abide, does not eat spiritually, and so takes the sacrament to himself bodily unto judgment.

*As the Father hath sent me.* He sent me, equal to himself; that is, he made me man, and thence it is that I refer my life to him as to one greater. *And he shall live.* That I live by the Father, my own emptying-out effects; that a man live by me, the participation effects which eats me.

echoes.text: The king answered, I know of a certainty that you would gain time, because you see the thing is gone from me.
echoes.note: 'You are trying to gain time' (kairon hymeis exagorazete) supplies the rare Septuagintal idiom behind 'redeeming the time' (ton kairon exagorazomenoi). Low volume but a genuine lexical parallel the prompt flags; contested because the sense is repurposed positively.

echoes.text: Therefore a prudent person keeps silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.
echoes.note: 'The prudent will keep silent in such a time, for it is an evil time' parallels 'redeeming the time, because the days are evil.' Coherence in the wise-conduct-in-an-evil-time motif; low volume and contested.

echoes.text: that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; that the man of understanding may attain to sound counsel:
echoes.note: The wise/unwise contrast and the call to 'understand' echo wisdom's exhortation to gain prudence. Faint; included for the walk-wisely paraenesis drawing on the wisdom tradition.

echoes.text: Don’t look at the wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly.
echoes.note: 'Do not look at wine when it is red... in the end it bites like a serpent' grounds the prohibition 'Do not be drunk with wine, in which is dissipation (asotia).' Coherence with the wisdom warning against drunkenness is strong; medium volume.

echoes.text: They also reel with wine, and stagger with strong drink. The priest and the prophet reel with strong drink. They are swallowed up by wine. They stagger with strong drink. They err in vision. They stumble in judgment.
echoes.note: 'They reel with wine and stagger with strong drink... they err in vision' supplies the prophetic picture of drunkenness as spiritual derangement, contrasted here with being filled with the Spirit. Medium coherence; the wine-versus-prophetic-Spirit antithesis is apt.

echoes.text: Sing to him a new song. Play skillfully with a shout of joy!
echoes.note: 'Sing to him a new song, play skillfully' stands behind 'psalms and hymns and spiritual songs... making melody in your heart.' The psalmos/odes vocabulary and the heart-singing motif show coherence with the psalter's worship language; medium volume.

echoes.text: Wine is a mocker, and beer is a brawler. Whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
echoes.note: 'Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler' reinforces the wisdom condemnation of drunkenness behind the prohibition. Low volume; a recurrent sapiential warning rather than a specific quotation.

echoes.text: Sing to Yahweh a new song! Sing to Yahweh, all the earth.
echoes.note: 'Sing to the LORD a new song' is the recurrent psalter summons that the trio of psalms/hymns/songs evokes. Low volume given many parallel psalm-headings (psalmos, hymnos, ode) in the Septuagint; flagged for recurrence.

echoes.text: I will bless Yahweh at all times. His praise will always be in my mouth.
echoes.note: 'I will bless the LORD at all times; his praise shall continually be in my mouth' parallels 'giving thanks always concerning all things.' Faint thematic coherence with continual thanksgiving; low confidence.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: The whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness; and the children of Israel said to them, “We wish that we had died by the hand of Yahweh in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the meat pots, when we ate our fill of bread, for you have brought us out into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.” Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain bread from the sky for you, and the […]
echoes.note: 'The Jews therefore murmured concerning him' (v.41,43) deliberately casts the audience as the wilderness generation that 'murmured against Moses and Aaron' over bread. High Volume and Coherence: the same verb-of-grumbling against the same gift (bread from heaven).

echoes.text: All your children shall be taught of Yahweh; and great shall be the peace of your children.
echoes.note: 'It is written in the prophets, They will all be taught by God' (v.45) formally cites Isaiah 54:13 ('all your children shall be taught by the LORD'). A second explicit citation in the chapter; high Volume.

echoes.text: The mixed multitude that was among them lusted exceedingly: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, “Who will give us flesh to eat? We remember the fish, which we ate in Egypt for nothing; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic; but now we have lost our appetite. There is nothing at all except this manna to look at.” The manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium. […]
echoes.note: 'Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died' (v.49) recalls the wilderness generation that craved, ate, and perished. The manna's described provision (Num 11:7-9) plus the death of that generation give Volume to Jesus' contrast with bread that lets one 'not die.'

echoes.text: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says Yahweh: I will put my law in their inward parts, and in their heart will I write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people: and they shall teach no more every man his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying, Know Yahweh; for they shall all know me, from their least to their greatest, says Yahweh: for I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin […]
echoes.note: 'They shall all know me, from the least to the greatest' (new-covenant interiority of divine teaching) reinforces the 'taught by God' citation and the drawing/learning that brings one to Jesus (vv.44-45). Strong Coherence as a secondary new-covenant source.

echoes.text: He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.”
echoes.note: 'Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God' (v.46) reprises the Mosaic axiom 'no one shall see me and live.' Coheres with John's recurring claim that the Son alone has seen God (cf. 1:18); moderate Volume here.

echoes.text: and you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month; and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it at evening. They shall take some of the blood, and put it on the two door posts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they shall eat it. They shall eat the flesh in that night, roasted with fire, and unleavened bread. They shall eat it with bitter herbs. Don’t eat it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roasted with […]
echoes.note: 'The bread which I will give for the life of the world is my flesh' (v.51), under the Passover frame, fuses bread with the slain paschal lamb whose flesh is eaten and whose blood saves. Typological Coherence prepares the eat-flesh scandal of the next pericope.

echoes.text: “‘Any man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who live as foreigners among them, who eats any kind of blood, I will set my face against that soul who eats blood, and will cut him off from among his people. For the life of the flesh is in the blood; and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life. Therefore I have said to the children of Israel, “No person […]
echoes.note: 'Drink his blood' (v.53) collides head-on with the absolute Levitical prohibition: 'I will set my face against any who eats blood... the life is in the blood.' The scandal of vv.52-53 is unintelligible without this law; high Volume and Coherence as the offense John exploits.

echoes.text: They shall eat the flesh in that night, roasted with fire, and unleavened bread. They shall eat it with bitter herbs.
echoes.note: 'They shall eat the flesh that night' — the paschal lamb whose flesh is consumed. Jesus' demand to eat his flesh, set 'at Passover,' identifies him as the lamb; high typological Coherence binding the discourse to the chapter's opening note (v.4).

echoes.text: But flesh with its life, that is, its blood, you shall not eat.
echoes.note: 'You shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood' is the primal Noachic blood prohibition predating Sinai, broadening the scandal of v.53 beyond Israel to a universal taboo. Adds Recurrence to the blood-prohibition background.

echoes.text: Only be sure that you don’t eat the blood; for the blood is the life. You shall not eat the life with the flesh.
echoes.note: 'Only be sure that you do not eat the blood, for the blood is the life' restates the prohibition with the life-in-the-blood rationale that John ironically affirms (the blood gives life). Reinforces the contested commandment behind the discourse.

echoes.text: They that eat me will yet be hungry; And those who drink me will yet be thirsty.
echoes.note: Wisdom's 'those who eat me... those who drink me' returns here with literal eating and drinking, deepening the Wisdom-banquet identification of Jesus. Coheres with v.35; the eat/drink pairing strengthens the Sirach link.

echoes.text: “Come, eat some of my bread, Drink some of the wine which I have mixed!
echoes.note: 'Eat of my bread and drink of the wine I have mixed' — Wisdom's bread-and-wine banquet underlies the flesh-as-food/blood-as-drink doubling of vv.53-56. Lower distinctiveness than the Leviticus collision but adds the sapiential meal frame.

echoes.text: Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain bread from the sky for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law, or not.
echoes.note: 'Not as our fathers ate the manna, and died' (v.58) closes the discourse by again invoking the heaven-bread of Exodus 16, now surpassed. Recurrence of the governing manna text rather than a fresh allusion.

notes.text: Her house — For the reception of her guests. Seven - Many pillars; whereby is intimated the beauty and stability of the church. Pillars - Prophets, and apostles, and ministers.
Killed — Made provision for the guests. Mingled - With water, as they used to do in those hot countries. Furnished - With all necessaries, and now waits for the guests.

Maidens — Her servants to invite the guests, ministers of the word whom he calls maidens for the decency of the parable; for wisdom being compared to a great princess, was fit to be attended upon by maidens. Highest places - From such high seats as those from which Judges delivered their sentences, and officers made proclamations.
Simple — Ignorant, and weak.

glossa.text:
*Wisdom hath built herself a house.* Because he had spoken sufficiently of the eternity of the divinity of Christ, etc., *as far as* because he raised up men severed from the love of the world to bear the fabric of the Church.

*Seven pillars.* Namely the Churches throughout the world, etc., *as far as* as though by supporting they held it together.
*Come, eat my bread.* The divinity and the humanity joined into one person of Christ, or, in the *bread* his body, in the *wine* his blood, wherewith we are filled at the altar.

*Forsake childishness.* After the banquet set forth he adds also the counsels of life, that those whom he refreshes with the mysteries of his incarnation received, he may equally instruct with the words of doctrine.

notes.text: Fear — Reverence, serve, and trust him: for fear is commonly put for all the parts of God's worship.
Life — A long and happy life, begun in this world and continued forever in the next. Good - In which he may enjoy good, prosperity or happiness.
Evil — From all manner of evil speaking, from all injurious, false and deceitful speeches.

Depart — From all sin. Do good - Be ready to perform all good offices to all men. Seek - Study by all means possible to live peaceable with all men. Pursue it - Do not only embrace it gladly when it is offered, but follow hard after it, when it seems to flee away from thee.

glossa.text: *All ye his saints.* ((CASS.)) No one, however well deserving, shall leave off from this, let him not presume upon security. *For.* ((AUG.)) The Lord was feeding him that despised him, and he will forsake him that fears him. But he promises not superfluous things, but necessary ones. *There is no want.* Because even in the present they have as much as nature requires.

*The rich have wanted and have suffered hunger.* ((CASS.)) Because they have not faith. *They have suffered hunger,* because they are not filled with the body of the Lord. For what have they who have not God? Or, *the rich have wanted,* that is, they shall lack the highest good, although they hunger, that is, desire. But those who seek with their whole zeal shall have without diminution the good which is every good.

*Come, children, hear me.* Diapsalmus. The sacraments of the Church having been treated, he admonishes those who are outside, who take the first rudiments of faith, lest the name of fear be shuddered at, he adds: *I will teach you,* the sons, the fear of the Lord, as a useful thing.

((CASS.)) Now he warns beginners also from what things they should abstain.
*To see good days.* Because all confess that they wish it.

*Keep.* ((ID.)) Note that he says the tongue is to be restrained first, since, when we wish to speak, we first move the lips, which the motions of the tongue soon follow. *Keep* thou who desirest life. Behold how they ought to fear.
*Turn away from evil.* ((CASS.)) This avoids fault, etc., *as far as* otherwise he will not be received in the world to come.

notes.text: Circumspectly — Exactly, with the utmost accuracy, getting to the highest pitch of every point of holiness. Not as fools - Who think not where they are going, or do not make the best of their way.

With all possible care redeeming the time — Saving all you can for the best purposes; buying every possible moment out of the hands of sin and Satan; out of the hands of sloth, ease, pleasure, worldly business; the more diligently, because the present are evil days, days of the grossest ignorance, immorality, and profaneness.
What the will of the Lord is — In every time, place, and circumstance.
Wherein is excess — That is, which leads to debauchery of every kind. But be ye filled with the Spirit - In all his graces, who gives a more noble pleasure than wine can do.

Speaking to each other — By the Spirit. In the Psalms - Of David. And hymns - Of praise. And spiritual songs - On any divine subject. By there being no inspired songs, peculiarly adapted to the Christian dispensation, as there were to the Jewish, it is evident that the promise of the Holy Ghost to believers, in the last days, was by his larger effusion to supply the lack of it. Singing with your hearts - As well as your voice. To the Lord - Jesus, who searcheth the heart.

Giving thanks — At all times and places. And for all things - Prosperous or adverse, since all work together for good. In the name of, or through, our Lord Jesus Christ - By whom we receive all good things.

glossa.text: *Redeeming the time.* That is, what you have done less in one time, restore in another, halving the days which the wicked do not halve. For some halve, others fill up the days, others do not even begin; that is, some die in Egypt, some in the desert, some in the holy land. Nor is it a wonder if you have done less, since the days are evil, nor can all things be done at pleasure.

Observe the degrees: the Jews are tried here; the disciples, ver. 60-66, the apostles, ver. 67.

This is — That is, I am the bread - Which is not like the manna your fathers ate, who died notwithstanding.

For human flesh, which was liable to sin and therefore dead, being united to his clean flesh, incorporated, made one with him, lives by his spirit, as the body lives by its own spirit: but he who is not of the body of Christ does not live by the spirit of Christ. But because the Jews were not of this unity, they strove; nor is it expounded to such men how the Lord gives his flesh to be eaten, but he heard, whence they are the more moved.

*Unless you eat the flesh,* etc. ((AUG.)) He wishes this food and drink to be understood as fellowship, etc., *as far as* that from many grains there may be one bread, and from many berries the wine flows together.

*He that eateth.* Certain holy men expound this of the eating of the altar, and they say well; but they ask how it may be unto life everlasting, since for some it is unto death, as the Apostle says. If any man eats at the altar with this eating of which he here treats, namely with faith working and with love, he eats unto life everlasting. But if any man eats otherwise, unto death.

*For the flesh.* Truly the soul and the body shall live from this food, because *my flesh is meat indeed.* Which alone makes men immortal, so that they shall neither hunger nor thirst; another food does not afford this, even if this be sought in it.

*He that eateth.* Now he expounds how that comes to pass which he said, and what it is to eat the flesh and to drink the blood: that is, to abide in Christ and to have Christ abiding in oneself. But he who does not abide in Christ, and in whom Christ does not abide, does not eat spiritually, and so takes the sacrament to himself bodily unto judgment.

*As the Father hath sent me.* He sent me, equal to himself; that is, he made me man, and thence it is that I refer my life to him as to one greater. *And he shall live.* That I live by the Father, my own emptying-out effects; that a man live by me, the participation effects which eats me.

echoes.text: The king answered, I know of a certainty that you would gain time, because you see the thing is gone from me.
echoes.note: 'You are trying to gain time' (kairon hymeis exagorazete) supplies the rare Septuagintal idiom behind 'redeeming the time' (ton kairon exagorazomenoi). Low volume but a genuine lexical parallel the prompt flags; contested because the sense is repurposed positively.

echoes.text: Therefore a prudent person keeps silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.
echoes.note: 'The prudent will keep silent in such a time, for it is an evil time' parallels 'redeeming the time, because the days are evil.' Coherence in the wise-conduct-in-an-evil-time motif; low volume and contested.

echoes.text: that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; that the man of understanding may attain to sound counsel:
echoes.note: The wise/unwise contrast and the call to 'understand' echo wisdom's exhortation to gain prudence. Faint; included for the walk-wisely paraenesis drawing on the wisdom tradition.

echoes.text: Don’t look at the wine when it is red, when it sparkles in the cup, when it goes down smoothly.
echoes.note: 'Do not look at wine when it is red... in the end it bites like a serpent' grounds the prohibition 'Do not be drunk with wine, in which is dissipation (asotia).' Coherence with the wisdom warning against drunkenness is strong; medium volume.

echoes.text: They also reel with wine, and stagger with strong drink. The priest and the prophet reel with strong drink. They are swallowed up by wine. They stagger with strong drink. They err in vision. They stumble in judgment.
echoes.note: 'They reel with wine and stagger with strong drink... they err in vision' supplies the prophetic picture of drunkenness as spiritual derangement, contrasted here with being filled with the Spirit. Medium coherence; the wine-versus-prophetic-Spirit antithesis is apt.

echoes.text: Sing to him a new song. Play skillfully with a shout of joy!
echoes.note: 'Sing to him a new song, play skillfully' stands behind 'psalms and hymns and spiritual songs... making melody in your heart.' The psalmos/odes vocabulary and the heart-singing motif show coherence with the psalter's worship language; medium volume.

echoes.text: Wine is a mocker, and beer is a brawler. Whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
echoes.note: 'Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler' reinforces the wisdom condemnation of drunkenness behind the prohibition. Low volume; a recurrent sapiential warning rather than a specific quotation.

echoes.text: Sing to Yahweh a new song! Sing to Yahweh, all the earth.
echoes.note: 'Sing to the LORD a new song' is the recurrent psalter summons that the trio of psalms/hymns/songs evokes. Low volume given many parallel psalm-headings (psalmos, hymnos, ode) in the Septuagint; flagged for recurrence.

echoes.text: I will bless Yahweh at all times. His praise will always be in my mouth.
echoes.note: 'I will bless the LORD at all times; his praise shall continually be in my mouth' parallels 'giving thanks always concerning all things.' Faint thematic coherence with continual thanksgiving; low confidence.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: The whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness; and the children of Israel said to them, “We wish that we had died by the hand of Yahweh in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the meat pots, when we ate our fill of bread, for you have brought us out into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.” Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain bread from the sky for you, and the […]
echoes.note: 'The Jews therefore murmured concerning him' (v.41,43) deliberately casts the audience as the wilderness generation that 'murmured against Moses and Aaron' over bread. High Volume and Coherence: the same verb-of-grumbling against the same gift (bread from heaven).

echoes.text: All your children shall be taught of Yahweh; and great shall be the peace of your children.
echoes.note: 'It is written in the prophets, They will all be taught by God' (v.45) formally cites Isaiah 54:13 ('all your children shall be taught by the LORD'). A second explicit citation in the chapter; high Volume.

echoes.text: The mixed multitude that was among them lusted exceedingly: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, “Who will give us flesh to eat? We remember the fish, which we ate in Egypt for nothing; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic; but now we have lost our appetite. There is nothing at all except this manna to look at.” The manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium. […]
echoes.note: 'Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died' (v.49) recalls the wilderness generation that craved, ate, and perished. The manna's described provision (Num 11:7-9) plus the death of that generation give Volume to Jesus' contrast with bread that lets one 'not die.'

echoes.text: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says Yahweh: I will put my law in their inward parts, and in their heart will I write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people: and they shall teach no more every man his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying, Know Yahweh; for they shall all know me, from their least to their greatest, says Yahweh: for I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin […]
echoes.note: 'They shall all know me, from the least to the greatest' (new-covenant interiority of divine teaching) reinforces the 'taught by God' citation and the drawing/learning that brings one to Jesus (vv.44-45). Strong Coherence as a secondary new-covenant source.

echoes.text: He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.”
echoes.note: 'Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God' (v.46) reprises the Mosaic axiom 'no one shall see me and live.' Coheres with John's recurring claim that the Son alone has seen God (cf. 1:18); moderate Volume here.

echoes.text: and you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month; and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it at evening. They shall take some of the blood, and put it on the two door posts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they shall eat it. They shall eat the flesh in that night, roasted with fire, and unleavened bread. They shall eat it with bitter herbs. Don’t eat it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roasted with […]
echoes.note: 'The bread which I will give for the life of the world is my flesh' (v.51), under the Passover frame, fuses bread with the slain paschal lamb whose flesh is eaten and whose blood saves. Typological Coherence prepares the eat-flesh scandal of the next pericope.

echoes.text: “‘Any man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who live as foreigners among them, who eats any kind of blood, I will set my face against that soul who eats blood, and will cut him off from among his people. For the life of the flesh is in the blood; and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life. Therefore I have said to the children of Israel, “No person […]
echoes.note: 'Drink his blood' (v.53) collides head-on with the absolute Levitical prohibition: 'I will set my face against any who eats blood... the life is in the blood.' The scandal of vv.52-53 is unintelligible without this law; high Volume and Coherence as the offense John exploits.

echoes.text: They shall eat the flesh in that night, roasted with fire, and unleavened bread. They shall eat it with bitter herbs.
echoes.note: 'They shall eat the flesh that night' — the paschal lamb whose flesh is consumed. Jesus' demand to eat his flesh, set 'at Passover,' identifies him as the lamb; high typological Coherence binding the discourse to the chapter's opening note (v.4).

echoes.text: But flesh with its life, that is, its blood, you shall not eat.
echoes.note: 'You shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood' is the primal Noachic blood prohibition predating Sinai, broadening the scandal of v.53 beyond Israel to a universal taboo. Adds Recurrence to the blood-prohibition background.

echoes.text: Only be sure that you don’t eat the blood; for the blood is the life. You shall not eat the life with the flesh.
echoes.note: 'Only be sure that you do not eat the blood, for the blood is the life' restates the prohibition with the life-in-the-blood rationale that John ironically affirms (the blood gives life). Reinforces the contested commandment behind the discourse.

echoes.text: They that eat me will yet be hungry; And those who drink me will yet be thirsty.
echoes.note: Wisdom's 'those who eat me... those who drink me' returns here with literal eating and drinking, deepening the Wisdom-banquet identification of Jesus. Coheres with v.35; the eat/drink pairing strengthens the Sirach link.

echoes.text: “Come, eat some of my bread, Drink some of the wine which I have mixed!
echoes.note: 'Eat of my bread and drink of the wine I have mixed' — Wisdom's bread-and-wine banquet underlies the flesh-as-food/blood-as-drink doubling of vv.53-56. Lower distinctiveness than the Leviticus collision but adds the sapiential meal frame.

echoes.text: Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain bread from the sky for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law, or not.
echoes.note: 'Not as our fathers ate the manna, and died' (v.58) closes the discourse by again invoking the heaven-bread of Exodus 16, now surpassed. Recurrence of the governing manna text rather than a fresh allusion.

lines: The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord.
We come with our whole hearts to learn.
Eat this bread, drink this cup, and abide in me.
And we will abide in him, and he in us.
Be filled with the Spirit; sing and make melody.
We come singing, with thanks in our hearts.
Come, all who hunger for life; come, let us worship.
We come to the table of the Lord. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Wisdom begins in awe, said the old psalm, and Solomon asked God not for riches but for a listening heart to know the good.
Give us this bread always.
The living bread is no mere idea: take and eat, take and drink, and the life of God runs in you the way blood runs in your veins.
Give us this bread always.
Those who eat this bread abide in Christ and Christ in them, at home in one another, the way a branch lives in the vine.
Give us this bread always.
So be filled, and sing; come to the table set for the hungry, and let your whole heart make melody to God.
Give us this bread always.
